page: Amazon Web Services m5ad.large is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro System architecture. It features an AMD EPYC 7571 x86_64 processor operating at 2.2 GHz, configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core via multithreading. Memory capacity is 8.0 GB of DDR4 running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. A key hardware attribute is the bundled 75 GB local NVMe SSD instance store, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. No hardware accelerators or GPUs are present on this instance type.

Benchmark evaluations reflect entry-tier processing performance consistent with older-generation AMD silicon. In synthetic CPU assessments, the instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 720.0 and a multi-core score of 955.0, alongside a PassMark CPU rating of 1854.08 and stress-ng throughput of 590.4. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 20.35 GB/sec, while write operations measure 11.91 GB/sec. In service workloads, the system delivers 1.26 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 1.58 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

Cost efficiency is driven by the integration of fast local NVMe storage combined with a modest dual-vCPU footprint. The local NVMe SSD provides low-latency ephemeral I/O without the bandwidth overhead and variable latency associated with networked block storage. The primary tradeoff is constrained processing headroom, which restricts throughput on parallel or compute-heavy pipelines. As a result, the m5ad.large is best suited for lightweight web serving, caching nodes, local build scratch space, and microservices requiring local ephemeral disk operations.
description: Amazon Web Services m5ad.large is a general-purpose cloud instance configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs and 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory, yielding a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it utilizes a 2.2 GHz AMD EPYC 7571 x86_64 processor across a single physical core with multithreading enabled. The instance integrates 75 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD storage and supports a 1 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate entry-tier processing capabilities, registering a Geekbench multi-core score of 955.0, a PassMark CPU score of 1854.08, and Redis throughput of 1.26 million operations per second. Memory bandwidth registers 20.35 GB/sec for uncached block reads. The instance provides an economical solution for caching tiers, development environments, and web application hosting where bundled NVMe temporary disk access is beneficial, though heavy computational tasks are limited by the small CPU footprint.
